blocks.text: 1  Research objective

Overall objective. When a model cannot remember everything it has seen, which observations should it keep? Our proposal tests whether the extra prediction error caused by deleting a memory can teach a small retention policy to make better choices.

runs.text: When a model cannot remember everything it has seen, which observations should it keep? Our proposal tests whether the extra prediction error caused by deleting a memory can teach a small retention policy to make better choices.

blocks.text: Objective of this stage. Establish the prerequisites before learning a policy: useful evidence must survive visual encoding, the predictor must respond to that evidence, and equal-sized memory alternatives must produce informative differences in prediction cost. The original Phase One covers the first two questions; the deletion assay is a transition toward the later retention stage.

blocks.text: 2  Experimental design
2.1  Data and preprocessing

We use generated, controlled visual trajectories rather than a public video benchmark. Each matched pair contains two episodes with identical recent images and action sequences, but different earlier evidence and later outcomes. Gate tests a transient cue; Motion tests pre-occlusion movement. Historical split names contain the word test, but these data are now development evidence because predictor repairs were informed by them.

blocks.text: Shared settings

The candidate starts with a frozen recent-only forecast and adds a learned correction from centered historical features. It reads every retained entry, weights their content, and uses elapsed time with observed feature differences to transport evidence forward. This is a prediction mechanism, not a trained memory-retention policy; no retrieval or selector chooses the stored entries.

runs.text: The candidate starts with a frozen recent-only forecast and adds a learned correction from centered historical features. It reads every retained entry, weights their content, and uses elapsed time with observed feature differences to transport evidence forward. This is a prediction mechanism, not a trained memory-retention policy; no retrieval or selector chooses the stored entries.

blocks.text: Recent context is 4 frames; the bounded history contains 2 real entries; future horizons are 3 and 6 steps. Full history is an additional information reference, not an equal-capacity competitor. The complete candidate experiment trained seeds 17, 29 and 43 for each task: six models, 120 epochs and 7680 steps each. Checkpoints were selected by the earliest minimum of validation MSE across four balanced conditions and both horizons.

blocks.text: Reading the numbers

MSE means average squared error: lower is better. A positive error reduction means history helped. For prediction tests, 95 percent confidence intervals use 2000 paired bootstrap replicates of 128 base pairs; the deletion assay uses 10000 replicates. Siblings, deletion forks and seed means are not additional independent examples. An uncertainty interval crossing zero leaves the direction unresolved.

blocks.text: Why exactly 50 and 100 percent. The original values are 0.5 and 1.0, not rounded approximations. Paired recent inputs are identical but their labels are opposite: the recent-only classifier gives the same answer to both, getting exactly one right. Historical inputs are explicitly chosen evidence frames, and a supervised linear readout has learned to decode them. It correctly classified all evaluated examples in these controlled conditions. This is an observed ceiling on a deliberately simple diagnostic, not guaranteed perfection on new data.

blocks.text: 4.1  What has been achieved

The pipeline preserves the relevant discrete evidence, and both predictors respond to its content. Gate has broad prediction coverage. Motion provides consistent deletion value and cross-horizon transfer, even though its long-occlusion forecast quality remains limited. This is meaningful mechanism evidence for a bounded-memory project, with task- and condition-specific limits.

blocks.text: Conclusion

Phase One has produced substantial but uneven evidence. Historical information survives encoding, the predictors use it, and Motion deletion costs consistently distinguish useful evidence in the tested pools. Gate deletion stability and Motion hard-condition prediction remain limitations. These findings support a scoped next-stage feasibility study, while leaving learned-policy advantage, V-JEPA transfer and independent confirmation unproven.
